segments.speaker: ANNIE
segments.en: Oh Ben - I just remembered I never filled in that form for Nick - did you do it?

segments.speaker: BEN
segments.en: The course feedback form?

segments.speaker: ANNIE
segments.en: Yes. If you want, we can do it together, I've got mine here.

segments.speaker: BEN
segments.en: Is that OK?

segments.speaker: ANNIE
segments.en: Yeah.

segments.speaker: BEN
segments.en: OK, let's have a look then. What do we have to do?

segments.speaker: ANNIE
segments.en: Let's fill in the top first, let's see, Course, Course code . ..

segments.speaker: BEN
segments.en: Er, it's Communication in Business.

segments.speaker: ANNIE
segments.en: OK, Communication . . . in . .. Business, I do know that, but what's the code?

segments.speaker: BEN
segments.en: CB 16 something, CB 162, isn't it?

segments.speaker: ANNIE
segments.en: Mmm, that's it, OK and dates, when did we start? I remember, my birthday's on May 4th and it was the day after, it must have been May 5th.

segments.speaker: BEN
segments.en: Gosh, doesn't seem that long ago, does it?

segments.speaker: ANNIE
segments.en: No, and we finish at the end of this week, on Friday, so that's July 15th?

segments.speaker: BEN
segments.en: Er .l.Qth, Monday was the 12th. Right, that was the easy bit, now let's have a look- "Please give your comments on the following aspects of the course", OK, what's the first one? Oh, course organisation. What do you think?

segments.speaker: ANNIE
segments.en: Er, clear? It was, wasn't it?

segments.speaker: BEN
segments.en: Yes, I think the organisation was clear. OK, anything else for course organisation?

segments.speaker: ANNIE
segments.en: It was a good thing he gave us the course outline at the beginning, in the first session, that was useful, so I'll put that down, shall I? Now, going on to suggestions for improvement, one thing that wasn't so good, I think we could have done a bit more work at the beginning, I mean at the beginning it seemed dead easy.

segments.speaker: BEN
segments.en: Yeah.

segments.speaker: ANNIE
segments.en: I thought it was going to be really easy and then all of a sudden in the second half of the course we got a whole load of work, reading to do and essays and things.

segments.speaker: BEN
segments.en: Yes, it'd be better if it was more even. OK, now course delivery, does that mean teaching?

segments.speaker: ANNIE
segments.en: Yeah, I suppose so. Well, what I thought was really good on this course was the standard of teaching. Actually - I mean some of the teachers were better than others - but the standard generally was fine. Much better than other courses I've been on.

segments.speaker: BEN
segments.en: Yeah, I agree. Let's put that then. What about suggestions for improvement?

segments.speaker: ANNIE
segments.en: I . .. I didn't think it was all that wonderful when we had great long grQ!ij2 discussion sessions that went on for hours and hours. I don't mean we shouldn't have group discussions, just that they shouldn't go on too long.

segments.speaker: ANNIE
segments.en: Now, on to materials and equipment.

segments.speaker: BEN
segments.en: Oh, now what was good about some sessions was the handouts.

segments.speaker: ANNIE
segments.en: Yes, I thought all the handouts were good actually, and some were great, with website addresses and everything.

segments.speaker: BEN
segments.en: One problem though with materials was the key texts.

segments.speaker: ANNIE
segments.en: Yes' There just weren't enough copies on reserve in the library. And if you can't get the key texts before the session, how are you supposed to do the reading? And not enough computers. You have to wait ages to get one.

segments.speaker: BEN
segments.en: OK, testing and evaluation - well, I don't know, it's hard to say until we've got our written assignments back.

segments.speaker: ANNIE
segments.en: Don't talk about it, I only got mine in yesterday, it was a real struggle. I hate to think what mark I'll get.

segments.speaker: BEN
segments.en: Yes, but at least we've done the oral presentation- I thought that was good, the way I got my feedback really quickly.

segments.speaker: ANNIE
segments.en: Yes, it was. And I liked the way we knew what we'd be evaluated on, we knew the criteria, so we knew we had to think about clarity, organisation, and so on.

segments.speaker: BEN
segments.en: Yeah, but I'm not so sure about the written work. One thing I think is that there's just too much, it's really stressful.

segments.speaker: ANN IE
segments.en: Yes, I'd agree and I don't see why they can't let us know the criteria they use for marking.

segments.speaker: BEN
segments.en: The written assignments? But he told us.

segments.speaker: ANNIE
segments.en: No, for the final exams. What are they looking for- what are the criteria? What makes a pass or a fail?

segments.speaker: BEN
segments.en: Yeah, I never thought of that. It'd be really useful.

segments.speaker: ANNIE
segments.en: OK, any other comments?

segments.speaker: BEN
segments.en: I thought student support was excellent.

segments.speaker: ANNIE
segments.en: Yeah, me too. OK, excellent. Other comments?

segments.speaker: BEN
segments.en: No, I can't think of anything else.

segments.speaker: ANNIE
segments.en: Nor me. OK, so that's done. Thanks, Ben.

segments.speaker: BEN
segments.en: No. thank you.
